request.prompt: A turkey vulture (Cathartes aura), one adult bird soaring in mid-air, long fairly narrow wings fully spread and held raised in a shallow V (dihedral), about 175 cm wingspan and 70 cm long, shaped to read from below and from above. Long parallel-edged wings with six long separated, fingered primary feathers at each blunt wingtip. Long rounded tail, spread, reaching well past the tucked legs. Tiny bare red head on a thin neck, barely projecting ahead of the wings, short ivory hooked bill. Blackish-brown body; underwing two-toned, black lining in front and silvery-grey flight feathers behind. Not an eagle, not a condor, no white ruff. Single bird, no base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.
